Info.title: Informações sobre GeoGami
Info.infotext1: GeoGami é um aplicativo para criar e jogar jogos baseados em mapas, especialmente adequado para uso em instituições educacionais. O aplicativo é acompanhado cientificamente e concebido didaticamente pelo Instituto de Geoinformática da Universidade Westfálische Wilhelms-Universität Münster.
Info.infotext2: O foco do GeoGami está em promover a competência de orientação baseada em mapas. Os criadores de jogos podem escolher entre tipos de tarefas correspondentes e apoiar os jogadores ativando ou desativando funcionalidades do mapa. GeoGami também é adequado para criar jogos temáticos, rallyes e excursões digitais.
Info.infotext3: Mais informações você encontra em nosso

content.0: In GeoGami you can play games created by yourself or by others. To see a list of games, choose 'Games' from the main menu, or scan a QR code if you have one.
content.1: Make sure 'Real world' is selected in the dropdown menu at the top, and choose between single- and multiplayer (single is the default). You can now search for your game. The map button at the bottom right lets you find games near you.
content.2: Once you have selected a game, enter your player name. To play GeoGami, the app uses your current GPS position but does not store it. If you give your consent, GPS and interaction data will be stored in a GDPR-compliant way (see 'Sharing data for teaching and research') and can later be used by the game's creator for analysis.

content.0: When creating a game, you can configure all conditions and difficulties yourself and tailor them to the players. Press 'Games' in the main menu to start.
content.1: A plus icon will now appear in the bottom right. Selecting it lets you create a new game. Choose 'Real world'.
content.2: Now create the tasks. The individual task types and an example are explained under the 'Task types' tab.

content.0: You can delete games you created if they are no longer needed. You can also edit them again if you noticed mistakes or want to change something.
content.1: After logging in, go to 'My games'. Note that only games matching the current game environment and mode are shown. Click the 'Edit' icon to the right of a game.
content.2: You can now edit, delete, or save the game. Editing looks the same as creating a new game and offers the same features.
content.3: Press the save icon at the top right to save. Enter the game name and location. If the tasks require it, the map section can be adjusted. Now save the game permanently.

content.0: Zoom: choose whether the zoom should be set to the task, to the game, by the player, or not at all.
content.1: Map section: choose whether the entire map section or a specific one is always visible, or whether the map section moves along with the player and can therefore shift.
content.2: Map rotation: set the orientation of the map (does the player always look up, or is north always at the top?)
content.3: Position marker: the position-marker setting changes the task significantly. If turned off, players have to orient themselves only by their surroundings to decide where they are. If turned on, they can orient themselves by the marker. If turned on only at the start of the task, they can orient themselves once at the start; if on demand, they can decide themselves how often they need this hint.
content.4: View-direction marker: the same notes apply as for the position marker. In addition, this marker shows not only the location but also the direction the player is facing. This feature only works if the position marker is enabled.
content.5: Track recording: when you enable track recording, players can see and follow their own movement live on the map. Children enjoy 'drawing' shapes like circles or hearts on the map. Track recording only refers to visualising on the map — in the background GeoGami always records the track.
content.6: Street highlighting: you can highlight the street section the player is currently on in red. Unlike the position marker, this does not reveal the exact position.
content.7: Highlight landmarks: use this to point out things in the landscape that, for example, can make orientation easier.

content.0:
Depending on the task type, you can configure further settings that improve the play experience or better address the goal of the task.
Enable or disable input confirmation: this controls whether players themselves have to confirm that they solved the task correctly.
content.1: Show flag: this sets the difficulty of the task by determining whether the destination flag is visible on the map.
content.2: Enable or disable feedback: this determines whether players immediately learn whether they solved the task correctly.
content.3: Keep flag on the map: this determines whether the destination of this task remains visible during the next tasks.
content.4: Enable multiple attempts: this determines whether players get a new chance if they solve the task incorrectly (only for thematic tasks).
content.5: Accuracy: set how close to the destination players must be to be considered 'in the right place'. Due to GPS inaccuracies, do not choose too small a distance.
content.6: Under Map features you can configure further settings for the position marker and for interaction with the map itself. These can be tried out under 'Learn' in the main menu.
content.7: Highlight landmarks: use this to point out things in the landscape that, for example, can make orientation easier.
